post.yt_title: The Bible Never Says Mary Magdalene Was a Prostitute #shorts
post.yt_desc:
The Bible never says Mary Magdalene was a prostitute. It says Jesus freed her: "Mary called Magdalene, out of whom had come seven demons" (Luke 8:2 NKJV).

The prostitute idea came from a sermon by Pope Gregory the Great in 591 AD that mixed her up with other women in the Gospels. Then the risen Jesus appeared to her first (Mark 16:9; John 20:14–17), and she told the disciples "that she had seen the Lord" (John 20:18 NKJV).

📖 Read it yourself: Luke 8:1–3 · John 20:11–18 (NKJV)

post.notes:
- Luke 8:2 NKJV quoted from "Mary called Magdalene" to the end of the verse ("…and certain women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities—" precedes; the sentence continues in v3), so the scroll shows … at both ends.
- John 20:18 NKJV: indirect speech; quoted "that she had seen the Lord" (verse continues ", and that He had spoken these things to her.").
- 591: Pope Gregory I, Homily 33 (preached 591), identified Mary Magdalene with the sinful woman of Luke 7 and Mary of Bethany. The Roman Catholic calendar revision of 1969 separated them.
- 'Appeared to her first': Mark 16:9 states it; John 20:11–18 narrates it. (Mark 16:9–20 is absent from the two oldest manuscripts; John's account alone supports the order.)
